headline: D-Wave Quantum and the chip maker SkyWater Technology have signed a multi-year agreement to keep making D-Wave's superconducting quantum chips at SkyWater's Minnesota factory.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: official announcement, new today, headline matches the facts; the release gives no price or end date.
importance_line: Quantum hardware makers depend on a few specialist chip factories, so a continued supply deal matters most to D-Wave and its customers, though the release gives no price, volume or end date and SkyWater is now owned by IonQ, another quantum company.
summary: SkyWater Technology, a US chip foundry that IonQ finished buying on 31 Jul 2026, and D-Wave Quantum said in a joint press release, published by The Quantum Insider, that they signed a multi-year agreement extending a partnership of more than a decade on making D-Wave's superconducting quantum processors. The release says the terms protect D-Wave's intellectual property, gives no financial terms, and adds that D-Wave's quantum computing technology cut lot delays at SkyWater's factory by up to 30% in an earlier maintenance-scheduling project.
notes: Pool source Data Center Dynamics blocked; The Quantum Insider's copy of the joint press release read instead. The IonQ ownership detail is not in the press release; it comes from IonQ's own release of 31 Jul 2026 ('IonQ Completes Acquisition of SkyWater Technology', read on ionq.com) and The Quantum Insider's company tag.
